title: Polynomial corners in finite fields beyond the distinct-degree case
summary: We prove a quantitative polynomial Roth theorem for corners in \(\mathbb F_p^2\) for arbitrary pairs of linearly independent polynomials. More precisely, given a positive integer $d$, there are constants $p_0$ and $C$ (depending only on $p$) so that for every $ p>p_0$, if polynomials \(φ_1,φ_2\in \mathbb \mathbb{F}_p [y]\) are of degree $\leq d$ vanishing at $0$ and are not linearly dependent, then every \(A\subset\mathbb F_p^2\) with $ |A|\ge C p^{2-1/14} $ contains a nontrivial corner $$ (x_1,x_2),\qquad (x_1+φ_1(y),x_2),\qquad (x_1,x_2+φ_2(y)) $$ for some \(y\in\mathbb F_p^\times\).
